issue: Later restricted decoder source and complexity qualification
clarification: The four resubmitted core files are byte-identical to published N780 and are not a new discovery. A separately preserved later wave adds exact fixed-degree partial-flag witness compilation, degree-promised model validation and persistent directed bad-item robust acquisition. Degree, fixed-tail/flag and corruption promises remain supplied; robust Monte Carlo wrong/UNKNOWN guarantees differ from the exact complete-class zero-semantic-error theorem. Current n16 and full-cube replays and final same-source RM controls are finite evidence, not universal advantage. The exact general capped bound remains D+(2T+2)P; its bare O(n^(d+1)) simplification needs fixed beta or a suitable growth restriction on log(1/beta). Degree-promised validation does not acquire the degree promise or contradict exact arbitrary-oracle recognition. See the new audit for guards, losses to controls, total source/bit costs and precise scope.

issue: Named sparse proposal conjecture refuted; decoder and other results retained
clarification: The continuation minimal-monomial conjecture S_p<=m Pr(F!=0), equivalently W<=m k for fair bits, is exactly refuted: g(OR4(A)-OR4(B)) has m=k=30 and W=1024>900 in every nontrivial finite abelian group. Growing/tensor OR families rule out every fixed multiplier and give an all-group lower exponent above1.12197. A paired-literal binary-matroid construction raises the lower exponent to log2(1+sqrt(2)) for GF(2) and groups with a nonzero order-two element; no such per-group claim is made for odd-order groups. A separately proved group-safe dyadic/support-dependent repair survives, including an all-group m^2 fallback. These are proposal-cost bounds for the named mixture; factored OR/matroid examples have easy direct samplers after their representation is supplied. The decoder and arbitrary conditional-sampling problem remain intact. Historical open-conjecture wording is retained as history; a source paired-literal arithmetic typo is explicitly corrected in the new proof.
